purpose: Quantify spatial aliases and the isolated effect of frequency-dependent delay in the existing 100 MHz band, without claiming a comparison between complete hardware receivers.
offsets: 31 active OFDM offsets plus the two nominal band edges -50 and +50 MHz
controls: Same quantized geometric delay codes in both models. True delay contributes exp(-j2pi f tau); the matched phase reference contributes exp(-j2pi fc tau). Equal amplitudes, same 64-element positions, no optimisation or learning.
normalization: Squared array-factor magnitude divided by 64 squared. Report 10log10 gains and TTD-minus-phase differences in dB at the prescribed steering direction.
scope: Isotropic planar-wave array calculation. Excludes multipath, DML transfer, detector noise, insertion-loss differences between hardware technologies and coding. No new BER result, no model training, no test-set-based selection.
checks: Exact equality of matched models at each centre frequency
Unity normalised broadside gain with zero delays
Unity broadside grating-lobe replicas at the analytically predicted 20 GHz azimuths
All delay codes lie within the existing 0..76 grid
Finite results for every predefined condition
reporting: Retain all deterministic grid results, including cases where the matched phase reference has greater directional gain. No statistical significance test for a deterministic enumeration. No change to existing simulator or receiver scores.
